purpose: determine why benchmark results might differ from production-shaped reliability results -- NOT to declare one corpus better than the other.

matrix.omnidocbench: Chinese-dominant (765 simplified + 13 traditional = 778/1651), English 755/1651, mixed 116/1651. ZERO Vietnamese.
matrix.production_corpus: English/Vietnamese only ({'vi': 64, 'en': 45}), the system's explicitly documented target population (docs/production-contract.md).
matrix.implication: production's OCR is configured ocr_languages=[en,vi] (no zh model) -- roughly half of OmniDocBench's content is in a language this system's PRODUCTION configuration was never built to recognize. This is not a system weakness measured fairly; it is a language mismatch, and per Phase 16/2's explicit instruction, was NOT worked around by adding zh (007 already showed that costs English 43.6% and collapses English table structure).

matrix.omnidocbench: book, PPT2PDF, academic_literature, exam_paper, colorful_textbook, newspaper, magazine, research_report, note, historical_document ({'book': 276, 'PPT2PDF': 253, 'academic_literature': 215, 'exam_paper': 193, 'colorful_textbook': 159, 'newspaper': 151, 'magazine': 149, 'research_report': 132, 'note': 118, 'historical_document': 5})
matrix.production_corpus: enterprise business documents: invoices, contracts, business licenses, certificates, purchase orders, technical reports (docs/production-contract.md target population)
matrix.implication: almost entirely disjoint document TYPES -- OmniDocBench measures general document understanding across publishing/academic/media genres; production measures enterprise transactional-document extraction. A system tuned for one is not expected to be optimal for the other by construction.

matrix.omnidocbench: 665 table regions across 1651 pages (~0.40/page), plus a dedicated table_hard subset (97 pages) with complex nested tables
matrix.production_corpus: 37/109 documents have >=1 expected table -- tables are a CENTRAL, deliberately-engineered hard-case category (029-033's entire research chain), not incidental content
matrix.implication: both corpora care about tables, but for different reasons: OmniDocBench samples table STRUCTURE diversity broadly; the production corpus specifically engineers table+stamp/occlusion INTERACTION, which OmniDocBench's attribute schema does not label at all (see 'stamps/occlusion' row).

matrix.omnidocbench: varied print quality, some historical documents with geometric_deformation/low-resolution special_issue tags
matrix.production_corpus: deliberately engineered hard cases: corrupt CMap encoding, low contrast, watermarks, rotated regions, small text (research/hardcases/, 14 EN/VI cases)
matrix.implication: both stress OCR, via different, largely non-overlapping mechanisms.

matrix.omnidocbench: NOT a labelled attribute anywhere in the page_attribute schema (data_source/language/layout/special_issue/subset -- none of these cover stamps or seals). special_issue values observed: watermark, geometric_deformation, others -- not stamp-specific.
matrix.production_corpus: THE central mechanism of 025/029/030/031's entire research chain -- 7 documents with table-shaped picture-labelled regions under stamps, 2 with a confirmed real route-driven table/picture flip (031).
matrix.implication: the single most production-critical phenomenon this research chain has found (table-label gating under stamps) has NO corresponding ground-truth attribute in OmniDocBench -- confirmed absent, not merely unmeasured (see cross_research_comparison.json Phase 10).

matrix.omnidocbench: not a distinct data_source or category_type (closest: 'text_block'/'table' categories generically) -- production-contract.md itself notes forms are 'not implemented' in this system, and 032/033 confirmed a real checkbox_selected/unselected label-mapping bug that has never manifested in any historical experiment artifact
matrix.production_corpus: present as isolated hard-case documents (ord_form_vi, hc_checkbox_vi -- found by 033's own negative_controls.json search) but NOT a scored capability
matrix.implication: neither corpus scores forms as a first-class capability; both would need new evidence to measure this properly.

matrix.omnidocbench: an explicit page_attribute value: layout in {single_column, 1andmore_column, other_layout} -- directly labelled and filterable
matrix.production_corpus: present but not a labelled attribute; production-contract.md rates multi-column 'good (100% text; ordering is the open question)'
matrix.implication: OmniDocBench can isolate multi-column performance directly via its own attribute filter; the production corpus cannot without manual re-labelling -- a genuine measurement capability OmniDocBench has that the internal corpus lacks.

matrix.omnidocbench: explicit layout_hard subset (99 pages) plus the layout attribute field
matrix.production_corpus: not a labelled dimension; complexity is implicit in which hard_case_labels a document carries
matrix.implication: same asymmetry as multi-column: OmniDocBench has a purpose-built difficulty axis here.

matrix.omnidocbench: rich: category_type per region (text_block, title, table, figure, equation_*, header/footer, etc.) -- OUTPUT-level (what SHOULD be in the final document), not internal-pipeline-level
matrix.production_corpus: no independent ground-truth region annotation at all -- 028-033's Layer-2 evaluation instead inspects THIS system's OWN produced IR directly (structural_integrity, recovery verdicts, etc.), with no external reference to compare against
matrix.implication: fundamentally different evaluation philosophies: OmniDocBench validates against an independent ground truth (external validity); 023-033 validates the SYSTEM'S OWN internal consistency and evidence integrity (reliability under its own logic) -- see cross_research_comparison.json.

matrix.omnidocbench: NONE -- the evaluator compares final predicted markdown/table/formula text against ground truth text; it has no concept of 'which token belongs to which region' ownership, duplication, or orphan evidence at all
matrix.production_corpus: THE central subject of 025/028/029's evidence-ownership research (orphan tokens, 82-token overlapping-ownership finding, duplicate emission)
matrix.implication: evidence ownership/duplication (Class B/C in the 023-033 taxonomy) is STRUCTURALLY invisible to OmniDocBench's methodology -- not a gap in this run, a gap in what any output-text-comparison benchmark CAN measure.

matrix.omnidocbench: none -- ground truth carries no notion of 'why' a region has its label; it IS the label
matrix.production_corpus: central to 031/032/033's provenance design work (source_backend, Element.extra, routing_decision) -- but this is a PRODUCTION IR property, not something any benchmark's ground truth would carry either
matrix.implication: not a meaningful comparison axis -- neither corpus's GROUND TRUTH has provenance; provenance is a property of THIS system's output, orthogonal to which input corpus is used.

conclusion: OmniDocBench and the production-shaped corpus are almost entirely complementary, not overlapping: OmniDocBench provides external validity on OUTPUT accuracy across a language/genre/layout distribution the production corpus never samples; the production corpus provides internal evidence-integrity validation (ownership, duplication, label-gating, role ambiguity) that OmniDocBench's output-only methodology cannot see by construction. A strong result on one says little about the other axis.
